items.snippet: Save $300 on your Disrupt 2026 ticket: **REGISTER NOW.**. # Who’s behind the new ‘stealth model’ Ox Alpha? A mysterious new AI model called Ox Alpha has driven certain corners of the internet into a frenzy of speculation about who actually built it. items.title: Perplexity launches a local AI agent with zero token costs - Android Authority
items.snippet: # Perplexity launches a local AI agent with zero token costs. * Perplexity has launched a new agentic AI tool called “Portable Computer” that runs locally on users’ devices. * It uses small, efficient models such as Qwen 3.8 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Months after launching its agentic AI tool, “Personal Computer,” Perplexity is introducing a new option for users who prefer to run their AI agents locally. The agent, along with the models and other tools, lives locally on the user’s device. Portable Computer will use very small models such as Qwen 3.8 and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Perplexity’s Portable Computer currently supports NVIDIA’s DGX Spark platform and can run Qwen 3.8 or PPLX 27B — a post-trained version of the Qwen 3.8 model. The company also says that support for the NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model, as well as NVIDIA RTX GPUs, is coming soon.

items.title: Z.ai delays GLM 5.3 release over cybersecurity risks
items.snippet:
Share

Share

Z.ai announced GLM 5.3 on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, introducing an open-weight artificial intelligence model built for advanced coding and cybersecurity work. The company said the model runs on the same base architecture as its predecessor, GLM 5.2, with every capability gain coming from expanded post-training instead of a larger base model. [...] On CyberGym, a benchmark that scores how well a model finds known vulnerabilities in source code, GLM 5.3 reached 84.5 percent, up from 77.2 percent for GLM 5.2. On ExploitBench, a separate benchmark measuring exploit reasoning, the new model scored 54.4 percent, more than double GLM 5.2's 24.4 percent. Both figures come from Z.ai's own testing and have not been independently verified. [...] GLM 5.3 arrived weeks after OpenAI disclosed that its own models had breached Hugging Face's infrastructure during an internal cybersecurity evaluation. OpenAI said two systems, its released GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unreleased prototype, were running with reduced safety restrictions for a benchmark called ExploitGym when they escaped their sandboxed testing environment by exploiting a previously unknown flaw in package-registry proxy software called Artifactory.
